plants.name: Aster novi-belgii
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial covered in daisy-like flower heads with yellow centers and narrow petals. It is a vital late-season nectar source for migrating monarch butterflies and native bees, and it is widely grown in gardens as well as found in wet meadows and along stream banks.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern North America; widely cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Aster comes from the Greek word for 'star', and the plant was once reclassified into the genus Symphyotrichum based on chromosome and DNA studies.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped pink-lilac flowers in autumn, before its leaves appear in spring. The blooms emerge directly from the soil without foliage, which has earned it the nickname 'naked ladies'. It grows in damp meadows and woodland edges and is popular in cottage gardens.
plants.location: Europe, from the British Isles to central Europe; naturalized in parts of North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a true crocus. It contains colchicine, a toxic compound that is also used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular semi-deciduous tree that blankets streets and parks with clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers as spring reaches full swing in the Southern Hemisphere. Its fern-like foliage and wide spreading canopy make it a favorite street tree in warm climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in South Africa, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacarandas turn the city purple each October, and it is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City'. Fallen blossoms create purple carpets on the pavement.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: A tall, airy annual with feathery foliage and saucer-shaped daisy-like flowers on slender stems. It thrives in sunny, warm conditions and blooms profusely until the first frost. In mild autumns it remains a bright garden fixture and attracts pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer to first frost (June to October)
plants.location: Native to Mexico; cultivated in gardens across the Americas, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Cosmos seeds were collected by Spanish priests in Mexico who grew them in mission gardens, and the name comes from the Greek 'kosmos', meaning order or harmony. In 2015 cosmos flowers were grown on the International Space Station.
